steps.tx: Severe **falciparum malaria** is treated with intravenous **artesunate**, 2.4 mg/kg at 0, 12, and 24 hours, then daily until the patient can take oral treatment. **Quinine** is the alternative only when artesunate is unavailable. Artesunate rapidly kills all circulating parasite stages, clearing parasitaemia significantly faster and lowering mortality compared to quinine.

Quinine is the alternative only when artesunate is unavailable. Artesunate rapidly kills all circulating parasite stages, clearing parasitaemia significantly faster and lowering mortality compared to quinine.

steps.tx: Severe malaria is known to cause **cerebral malaria**, shock, acidosis, severe anaemia, **hypoglycaemia**, renal failure, and pulmonary oedema. Hypoglycaemia is checked often because quinine and the disease both cause it. Cytoadherence and microvascular sequestration of parasitised erythrocytes in cerebral capillaries produce coma and uncal herniation.
steps.say: Severe malaria is known to cause cerebral malaria, shock, acidosis, severe anaemia, hypoglycaemia, renal failure, and pulmonary oedema. Hypoglycaemia is checked often because quinine and the disease both cause it. Cytoadherence and microvascular sequestration of parasitised erythrocytes in cerebral capillaries produce coma and uncal herniation.

rows: Maintain airway; avoid steroids or mannitol
Hyperinsulinaemia from quinine and parasite consumption
Serial blood glucose checks every 4 hours

steps.tx: Severe **dengue** leaks plasma. Fluid is titrated to perfusion and haematocrit, and it is stopped when the leak reverses, or the patient is pushed into **pulmonary oedema**. There is no routine bolus for every high haematocrit. Plasma leakage is transient and self-limiting, typically resolving within forty-eight hours of defervescence.

There is no routine bolus for every high haematocrit. Plasma leakage is transient and self-limiting, typically resolving within forty-eight hours of defervescence.

left.title: Critical leakage phase
points: Marked by rising haematocrit and pleural effusions
Titrate crystalloids to maintain urine output 0.5 mL/kg/h
Use colloids only for refractory profound shock

steps.tx: **Scrub typhus** is treated with **doxycycline**. An **eschar** is useful when present and is often absent. Delay in doxycycline is what makes the ICU course, not a missing eschar. Orientia tsutsugamushi induces widespread endothelial vasculitis, resulting in severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, acute kidney injury, and distributive shock.

Orientia tsutsugamushi induces widespread endothelial vasculitis, resulting in severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, acute kidney injury, and distributive shock.

rows: Search axilla, groin, and flexural folds
Start empiric doxycycline 100 mg twice daily
Safe option in pregnancy and severe intolerance

steps.tx: **Leptospirosis** with Weil disease or **pulmonary haemorrhage** is treated with penicillin or ceftriaxone, plus support of the lung and the kidney. **Conjunctival suffusion** and calf tenderness are clinical clues. Leptospiral toxin damages alveolar capillary membranes, triggering catastrophic intra-alveolar haemorrhage requiring urgent protective lung mechanical ventilation.

Conjunctival suffusion and calf tenderness are clinical clues. Leptospiral toxin damages alveolar capillary membranes, triggering catastrophic intra-alveolar haemorrhage requiring urgent protective lung mechanical ventilation.

left.title: Severe pulmonary leptospirosis
points: Presents with haemoptysis and bilateral alveolar infiltrates
Rapidly progresses to asphyxiating diffuse haemorrhage
Requires early lung protective mechanical ventilation

right.title: Weil disease manifestation
points: Classic triad of jaundice, renal failure and bleeding
Conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia out of proportion to transaminases
Treat with intravenous ceftriaxone or penicillin G

steps.tx: **Melioidosis**, Burkholderia pseudomallei, needs prolonged **eradication** after the intensive phase. It is in the differential of community sepsis in endemic districts, and ordinary short course antibiotics relapse. Initial therapy with intravenous ceftazidime or meropenem must be followed by oral co-trimoxazole for three to six months.
steps.say: Melioidosis, Burkholderia pseudomallei, needs prolonged eradication after the intensive phase. It is in the differential of community sepsis in endemic districts, and ordinary short course antibiotics relapse. Initial therapy with intravenous ceftazidime or meropenem must be followed by oral co-trimoxazole for three to six months.

rows: At least 14 days IV (longer if deep abscess)
Ceftazidime 2 g IV 8-hourly or meropenem 1 g IV 8-hourly
Oral co-trimoxazole plus folic acid to prevent relapse

steps.tx: **Tetanus** autonomic storms are treated in a quiet room, with **magnesium**, benzodiazepines, and wound care. **Metronidazole** is preferred to penicillin. Human tetanus immunoglobulin neutralises unbound toxin. Tetanospasmin permanently blocks inhibitory GABA and glycine release, producing severe muscle rigidity and profound sympathetic overactivity.

Human tetanus immunoglobulin neutralises unbound toxin. Tetanospasmin permanently blocks inhibitory GABA and glycine release, producing severe muscle rigidity and profound sympathetic overactivity.

left.title: Autonomic storm control
points: Intravenous magnesium sulfate infusion targets 2 to 4 mmol/L
High-dose diazepam or midazolam controls severe spasms
Early elective tracheostomy secures compromised airway

right.title: Etiological eradication
points: Metronidazole 500 mg IV 8-hourly clears Clostridium tetani
Human tetanus immunoglobulin 3000 to 6000 units IM
Surgical wound debridement removes toxin source

steps.tx: **Rabies** encephalitic disease is fatal once it is clinically established. ICU care is palliative unless the case meets a published treatment protocol in a specialist centre. **Post exposure prophylaxis** is the intervention that works, and it is given before symptoms. Immediate wound washing, vaccine, and rabies immunoglobulin prevent central nervous system invasion.
